newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends at new low on high oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends at new low on high oil prices.

text.p: A dearth of dollars created by high oil prices pushed the Sri Lanka rupee to a new closing low of 57.05 to the dollar, dealers said.
The previous closing low was 57.03 set on Monday.
"The market was very thin due to a lack of dollars, which led to the (U.S.) currency gaining even on slight import covering demand," said a Seylan Bank dealer.
The market was short of dollars as banks held on to the U.S. unit after it gained sharply overseas as oil prices reached near six-year highs, he said.
The overnight call money rate closed at 14 percent against Monday's 15 percent, with the market well supplied, dealers said.
"Low overnight call money cuts the cost of holding dollars, which is another reason for the shortage," said a Commercial Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by one local cent and fixed buying and selling rates at 55.9425 and 57.0726.
Dealers said they expected the Central Bank to push up the dollar aggressively tomorrow due to its sharp overseas gains, particularly versus the yen. - Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
